raw:
**PR #4 / US-01-02, spec-compliance review round 2: NOT COMPLIANT. Two blocking items, both on the same rule as round-1 B1 (a question with more than one right answer).**

Round-1 B1 (3p-40) is fixed. "What do we blow out on a birthday cake?" and "Co zdmuchujemy na torcie urodzinowym?" each have one answer, candles, and the record row matches the deck. Nothing in code or tests broke.

The blocking items:
- **3p-21 (new wording):** "What moves with you on the ground when the sun shines?" can also be answered "my feet".
- **3p-05 (unchanged since round 1, I missed it then):** "What do you brush your teeth with?" can also be answered "toothpaste".

The record marks "One answer: pass" for both, so criterion 4 / MOD-01-F14 is still not met.

**CI on 51d99c8** (run 38573011198, "Acceptance tests (Android 12 emulator)"): **completed / success**. The og-test-results artifact holds:
- **junit/unit.xml:** 51 tests, 0 failures.
  - AC-01-02-1: 4 pass
  - AC-01-02-2: 4 pass
  - AC-01-02-3: 5 pass
  - AC-01-02-4: 3 pass, including the new step 2 that compares Polish and English
  - AC-01-02-5: 16 pass, including the new step 3 for a repeated question text
  - AC-01-02-6: 3 pass
  - AC-01-02-7: 1 pass
- **junit/release.xml:** 7/7 pass, including the renamed "AC-01-02-7 step 2 — the release APK's embedded JavaScript bundle holds every deck's questions and answers, in Polish and English".
- **Maestro:** TC-00-01, TC-00-03, TC-01-01 and AC-01-01-4 (release build, offline) pass.
- **TC-01-02:** not in the run. DEC-44/46 defer it to US-03-01, so it is not a finding.

**Local checks:**
- **Run test-runs/2026-10-14_153132** (API 32): taken on 51d99c8 with a clean tree. `release/bundle-content.txt` reads "3+: 250 of 250 texts found in the bundle". 15 suites and 51 tests green.
- **My own run on the head:** `jest tests/unit` gives 8 suites and 38 tests green. `tsc`, `lint` and `format:check` are clean.
- **PR body vs record:** the record rows in the PR body are identical to `docs/delivery/content-checks/US-01-02-3-plus.md`.

**I checked every reworded question against the four Q29 checks and MOD-01-F07 in both languages.** For each one the record row matches the deck.
- **Clean:** 3p-01 lemon, 3p-20 lamp or pillow, 3p-29 (pl), 3p-34 (en, round-1 N4 done), 3p-37 pig, 3p-40, 3p-41 fridge, 3p-42 (pl), 3p-48 scarf (round-1 N1 done).
- **Problems:** 3p-21 (B1); 3p-25, a small shift in meaning between the languages (N4); 3p-44, borderline (N3).
- **Round-1 N3 and N10:** done.
- **Round-1 N5, N6, N8, N9:** still open (listed below as N7–N10).

## Criteria
| # | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | MET | 50 questions with pl/en; AC-01-02-1 passes in CI |
| 2 | MET | `src/content/checks.ts:43-57`; AC-01-02-2 passes in CI |
| 3 | MET | 13/12/13/12 per kind; AC-01-02-3 passes in CI |
| 4 | NOT MET | The record exists, is in the PR, compares both languages and passes in CI. But the 3p-21 and 3p-05 rows record a false "One answer: pass" (B1, B2). |
| 5 | MET | `checkDecks(decks)` returns []. Each breakage fails, including the new repeated-text case. Caveat: N1. |
| 6 | MET | AC-01-02-6 passes in CI; not touched in round 2 |
| 7 | MET | AC-01-02-7 unit test, plus the release-bundle check passes in CI and locally (250/250). TC-01-02 is deferred (DEC-44/46). |

## Covers
- **F02–F05, F09–F12, F15:** MET, with the same evidence as criteria 1–3 and 5–7.
- **F06:** MET.
- **F07:** MET. The record now shows both languages, and AC-01-02-4 step 2 compares both; the only gap is a small wording difference in 3p-25 (N4).
- **F14:** NOT MET (B1, B2).

## Other checks
- **Edge cases:** both are tested in AC-01-02-5 step 2 (counts above and below 50, a missing answer or question in either language, lengths over the limit).
- **Out of scope:** no violations. Round 2 touches only the deck, the record, `checks.ts`, tests, the derived AC docs and one case name in `test-acceptance.sh`.
- **Constitution:** no violations.

## Findings
- **B1 — `src/content/decks/3-plus.json:246` (3p-21); `docs/delivery/content-checks/US-01-02-3-plus.md:36`.**
  - Scenario: "What moves with you on the ground when the sun shines?" / "Co rusza się razem z tobą po ziemi, gdy świeci słońce?" A child answers "my feet" / "nogi" (or shoes, or the dog) and is told the answer is "Your shadow". The record's own rule is that "a child, or a parent reading it aloud, cannot give another correct one", yet it marks One answer: pass.
  - Fix: reword so only the shadow fits, e.g. en "What on the ground looks like you when the sun shines?" / pl "Co na ziemi wygląda jak ty, gdy świeci słońce?". Keep "dark" out (round-1 N2), then update the record row.
- **B2 — `src/content/decks/3-plus.json:54` (3p-05); record line 20.**
  - Scenario: "What do you brush your teeth with?" / "Czym myjesz zęby?" A child answers "toothpaste" / "pastą", which is correct, and is told it is "A toothbrush". The record marks One answer: pass. Same defect class as round-1 B1. It was already there in round 1 and I missed it.
  - Fix: e.g. en "What do we put toothpaste on to brush our teeth?" / pl "Na co nakładamy pastę, żeby umyć zęby?", answer "A toothbrush." / "Na szczoteczkę.". Or a choice: "a toothbrush or a spoon". Then update the row.
- **N1 — `tests/unit/AC-01-02-5-content-checks.test.ts:90-92`: the duplicate-category case no longer tests the category check.**
  - `other` is a copy with the same question texts. I ran `checkDecks([threePlus, other])` on scratch copies and it returns 101 problems: 100 repeated texts and 1 repeated category.
  - So if the category check at `checks.ts:80-82` were deleted, step 3 would stay green. That gap is in the guard US-01-03/04 rely on.
  - Fix: assert `toContain('category 3+ appears in more than one deck')`, or give `other` distinct texts.
- **N2 — `src/content/checks.ts:86-92`:** when two questions lack the same language, it also reports `en question "undefined" appears more than once` (reproduced). This is noise on top of the real "no en question" problems. Fix: filter out non-text values before `seen`.
- **N3 — `3-plus.json:522` (3p-44):** "What do we call the food we eat in the morning?" / "Jak nazywamy jedzenie, które jemy rano?" invites "cereal" / "płatki" / "kanapki". The old "Which meal…" was clearer. Borderline under the one-answer check; consider "Jak nazywa się posiłek rano?", or keep it and note why.
- **N4 — `3-plus.json:294` (3p-25), MOD-01-F07:** en "a pot of very hot water" vs pl "garnkiem z gorącą wodą" (just "hot"). The meaning shifts slightly. Fix: drop "very", or write "bardzo gorącą".
- **N5 — weaker one-answer edges (not changed in round 2):**
  - `3-plus.json:186` (3p-16): water from the clouds could also be snow or hail.
  - `3-plus.json:462` (3p-39): before shoes, a child could say tights / rajstopy.
  - Consider tightening both, or accepting them explicitly.
- **N6 — PR #4 body is stale:**
  - "Changes" says "unique ids and categories", and evidence #5 says "duplicate id/category caught". Neither mentions the new repeated-question-text check.
  - The impact text still says the record parser uses "English columns".
  - The evidence table cites only the local run. It should cite CI run 38573011198 (green on 51d99c8). This carries round-1 N9.
- **N7 — `src/content/checks.ts:21-23` (round-1 N5, still open):** any non-empty category label passes.
- **N8 — `src/content/checks.ts:30-58` (round-1 N6, still open):** unknown keys pass, so a misspelt "ilustration" is dropped silently.
- **N9 — `docs/specs/DECISIONS.md:570` (round-1 N8, still open):** DEC-46 lists `constitution.md` under Affects, but the constitution is unchanged.
- **N10 — `tests/unit/AC-01-02-4-age-suitability-record.test.js:19,42`:** `slice(2, 10)` cuts off any extra column. A row with a fifth check cell reading `fail` would still pass step 3. Fix: take `cells.slice(2, -1)` and require exactly 8 cells.

- /Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/docs/delivery/content-checks/US-01-02-3-plus.md
- /Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/src/content/checks.ts
- /Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/tests/unit/AC-01-02-5-content-checks.test.ts
- /Users/sulo/workspace/knowledge-quiz/tests/unit/AC-01-02-4-age-suitability-record.test.js
